cited_case_name: Whether the earlier finding in State of Maharashtra v. Ramesh Kumar
context: The larger bench held that the earlier decision failed to adequately weigh the absence of premeditation and that a single reflexive blow during a mutual scuffle, without evidence of intention to cause death or an injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, does not satisfy Section 300 IPC. The 2018 decision on this point is overruled. Conviction under Section 302 IPC set aside; conviction substituted under Section 304 Part II IPC.

cited_case_name: Applying the principle in Anita Verma v. State of Delhi
context: Applying the principle in Anita Verma v. State of Delhi (2019), the Court held that a civil dispute over repayment does not, without evidence of dishonest inducement at inception, become a criminal offence. The complaint disclosed a purely civil wrong. Proceedings under Section 420 IPC quashed.

cited_case_name: IPC in Anita Verma v. State of Delhi
context: The Court held that the principles governing dishonest inducement at inception, as developed under the erstwhile Section 415/420 IPC in Anita Verma v. State of Delhi (2019), continue to apply under the corresponding Section 316/318 BNS provisions, since the substantive definition is materially unchanged. Conviction under Section 318(4) BNS upheld.

cited_case_name: Following Meera Joshi v. State of Karnataka
context: Following Meera Joshi v. State of Karnataka (2024) and the underlying reasoning in Anita Verma v. State of Delhi (2019), the Court held that delay in repayment of a genuine commercial advance, without dishonest inducement at inception, does not amount to cheating. Proceedings under Section 318(4) BNS quashed.

cited_case_name: Whether the principle in Ghanshyam Das v. State of Rajasthan
context: The Court followed Ghanshyam Das v. State of Rajasthan (2010), holding that the principle that a reliable, trustworthy and consistent testimony of the survivor needs no corroboration remains good law and was not disturbed by any subsequent decision. Conviction under Section 376 IPC upheld.

cited_case_name: IPC in Prakash Chandra v. State of Haryana
context: The Court held that Section 108 BNS reproduces Section 306 IPC without material change, and the requirement of a proximate act or instigation, as laid down in Prakash Chandra v. State of Haryana (2016), continues to govern. Conviction under Section 108 BNS set aside for lack of proximate instigation; conviction under Section 85 BNS (cruelty) maintained.
